title: 64 years old 3 days compounds focused Upper Lower program review
summary: NH reviews a 3-day compound-focused program from a 64-year-old subscriber who benches 225, squats 315 and deadlifts 325. He keeps the frequency but trims redundant pressing and the many static 5x5s, suggests evolving rep ranges and higher reps for isolation, adds arm and rear delt isolation via supersets, and rebalances the Friday arm day into Monday plus a light second lower-body stimulus.
claims: Seeing a 64-year-old still lifting heavy compounds is proof that diligent, smart training can last a lifetime
At 64 recovery ability is lower, so frequency and volume must be managed carefully; this doesn't mean people over 40 must drop volume
Staying physically active is the key to staying young; his 91-year-old grandfather still works in the field and cuts trees
Benching 225, squatting 315 and deadlifting 325 lb at 64 is impressive
Intermediate to advanced lifters should usually train more than three times a week, but three is justified at 64 for recovery
Incline bench, bench and dips in one session repeat the same pattern; keep one of bench or dips, or rotate them weekly, and raise volume on the one kept
Chin-ups train antagonist muscles so they could be supersetted without hurting pressing performance
Evolving rep ranges such as 3-5 sets of 3-5 reps would usually mean less volume than a fixed 5x5 and help recovery as you age
Add curls, long-head triceps extensions and rear delt isolation; they cost little recovery, help prehab, and can be supersetted
5x10 on calves is fine because calves don't need high intensity; volume matters more for them
Many static 5x5s imply sandbagging; something like 5 sets of 3-5 for squats and 3-4 sets of 8-12 for upright rows lets you touch more intensity
Squats plus stiff-leg deadlifts can be rough on the lower back; rotate in Romanian deadlifts
Stiff-leg deadlifts work best around 6-10 reps rather than 5x5
If you can do 5x5 Pendlay rows you're sandbagging early sets; they also tax the lower back after squats
With lower back issues, replace Pendlay rows with rows that don't tax the lower back: ring rows, seal rows, dumbbell rows
A program needs some stretch-emphasis movements such as Romanian deadlifts or dumbbell rows
5x5 is not recommended for isolation movements
A Friday piling arm and shoulder work in many 5x5s is unmanaged junk volume; move some movements to Monday
5x5 is too much deadlift volume for most people; one set of five or 3x3 is better, especially with age
Add a light second lower stimulus on the upper day, e.g. light lunges or squats supersetted with RDLs or hyperextensions, and train calves again
Separate two similar strength lifts like incline bench and dips with other work so you're fresher for the second
